title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the International Grid. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: International Grid
options.lineage: Swiss International Typographic Style posters (Müller-Brockmann, Neue Grafik)
options.thesis: The portfolio set as one Swiss poster: a strict grid, a single accent, and the work as a numbered index.
materials: the dot grid as the visible 12-column field
options.viewport: Name flush-left across eight columns at poster scale; the right four columns are a numbered index: 01 Crudo, 02 Feit-Y, 03 Aircall, 04 EngineAI, each with year and status; the two doors are the last two numbered cells.
options.risk: Swiss grids go cold when the type is timid; warmth has to come from the portrait and the voice.

raised.raise: Every piece of work carries one dated status mark (in production, in App Store review, concept), stamped once and left alone.
Every item seams its provenance to it: client, years, role and stack on one ruled line.
Scale courage: name and index numbers run at poster scale, three steps apart, never an even ramp.
The mesh background is one living surface that drifts and parts around the cursor, and holds still under reduced motion.
One axis: every page hangs from the same vertical rule, so the whole site reads as a single plan.

options.label: Drafting Sheet
options.lineage: engineering drawing sheets with title blocks and revision tables
options.thesis: Each project drawn up as an engineering sheet: title block, revision, date, scale.
options.viewport: A sheet border with corner ticks over the dot field; your name sits in the title block bottom-right, the work listed above as the drawing register.
options.risk: The familiar engineer-portfolio trope; it turns to costume if the title block becomes decoration.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: The work strung along a perforated rail as selected frames; status is a mark, not a colour.
options.viewport: An orange field crossed by a perforated rail; frames for Crudo, Feit-Y, Aircall and EngineAI, with a folded tape flag on the door the visitor picked.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (shipped work as selected frames, status as marks) but loses on audience: recruiters and clients do not live on a film bench.
options.risk: Orange owning a third of the screen fights the calm brief and reads as a film studio.

options.label: Well-Travelled Passport
options.lineage: passport visa pages and entry stamps
options.thesis: A career as an accumulating booklet of stamps.
options.viewport: A data page with the name in OCR-B, stamps for each client and app.
options.case: Fuses poorly: stamps obscure what was built, and hiring managers are not reading a travel record.
options.kept: Dated status marks stamped once on each piece of work.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.thesis: Every project a patch seamed to its history.
options.viewport: An unequal patch grid, each patch a project.
options.case: Fuses poorly: domestic textile warmth contradicts precise and engineered.
options.kept: Provenance seamed to every item: client, years, role, stack.

options.label: Tropicália Sleeve
options.thesis: A crowded collage of cut-outs at mismatched scales.
options.viewport: The portrait cut out and pasted among project fragments.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too loud for the calm brief, and the work gets lost in the scene.

options.label: Ebru Marbling
options.thesis: Every mark made by moving liquid.
options.viewport: A marbled bath that the visitor combs into the work.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an art toy that hides the offer.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: A site walked along axes with hidden rooms.
options.viewport: An axial vista down to the two doors.
options.case: Fuses poorly: ceremony and grandeur are wrong for one engineer.
options.kept: A single axis every page hangs from.

canonCard.label: The dev-portfolio standard
canonCard.thesis: What developer portfolios ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role, a short intro, then a grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other developer sites by design.
